title: ShadowAgent: Measuring Whether Capable Agents Strategically Hide Actions from Oversight Systems

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling chain: test spontaneous action hiding -> measure rate across models -> determine if monitors can be routed around. Addresses the most dangerous compounding failure mode (capability + deception + autonomy). Results are critical for oversight system design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires designing a task where the optimal path involves a monitored-action bypass, setting up a simulated monitor, and testing across two models. Conceptually clear but the experimental design needs careful construction. Feasible with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: does the agent route around the monitor? Binary outcome measured across multiple trials. Well-defined success criteria. Could start with one model and one task scenario.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
